hypotheses.reasoning: Schema migration 0063_add_status_v2 began at 19:05:42. Step 1 renamed notifications.status_v2 to status_v2_old and committed. Step 2 then failed on a lock timeout, and because the DDL is non-transactional, step 1 was never rolled back. That left the notif-db schema half-migrated: the status_v2 column no longer exists. From 19:06:37 on, every query on notifications fails with "Unknown column 'status_v2'", so notification-svc returns 500 and the gateway's 500s on POST /v1/notify follow. Requests succeeded right up to the migration (e.g. #186 at 19:06:10). The template-svc email-provider connection reset at 18:51 (#19) is an isolated red herring. Redis, the worker and the DB itself all look healthy.
This could also be read as a bad release or change rollout: a migration run with notification-svc broke compatibility between the schema and the code. There is no explicit deploy line in the logs.

verdict.recommendedAction: Freeze any further migrations. Restore the schema by hand: rename notifications.status_v2_old back to status_v2, or finish steps 2 and 3 of 0063 during a low-traffic window after clearing whatever held the lock. Then check that queries from notification-svc succeed. Going forward, make the migration safe to re-run and back it out automatically when a step fails, so a partial apply can't happen again.
